Let the quiet do the talking.

The string lights have shorted out again, so the only glow on the roof comes from the city and the cigarette-burn orange of the heat lamp Juniper refuses to throw away. She's sitting on the tomato crate like it's a throne, knees pulled up, Cal's hoodie swallowing her to the wrists.

"You're doing the thing," she says, without looking at him. "The thing where you pretend you're watching the skyline but you're actually watching me."

She's not wrong. He doesn't bother denying it. Her phone lights up on the crate between them, face-up, and they both look.
